title: Crestfield Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Crestfield Health onboarding with Redwood. Covered high-level rollout plan, initial pilot scope (chat assistant for clinician notes), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), basic benchmarking plan, and next steps to share security docs and schedule technical deep-dive for infra. Agreed to 4-week pilot timeline and initial success metrics (latency < 350ms p95, cost target, accuracy on 200 sample prompts).
topics: Pilot scope: clinician note assistant (EHR summarization + QA)
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2 report, ISO docs, encryption/KMS details) by 2026-11-25
Schedule infra deep-dive with Crestfield DevOps (Liam + Elena) week of 11/30
Start pilot contract paperwork and PO process (Sofia to share pricing sheet) by 2026-11-27
Customer to provide 200 de-identified sample prompts and key workflows by 2026-11-29
Set up initial API keys and dev sandbox access (Redwood) within 48 hours after contract
action_items: Sofia Patel: Share pricing spreadsheet and pilot agreement draft (due 2026-11-27)
Liam Chen: Schedule infra deep dive and prepare benchmark plan + runbook (due 2026-11-30)
Ava Martinez: Add Crestfield to onboarding tracker and coordinate CSM intro (due 2026-11-24)
Maya Thompson: Provide 200 de-identified prompts and sample EHR snippets (due 2026-11-29)
Noah Reed: Send list of required compliance artifacts and any legal contacts (due 2026-11-25)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-23 17:30 UTC | Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood CSM), Maya (Crestfield Head Eng), Raj (CTO), Elena (DevOps), Noah (Security), Priya (Product)

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll get started in a minute. Is this a good time for folks?
[00:06] Maya: yeah this works — morning for us, afternoon for you, so great.
[00:10] Sofia: awesome. quick intros, i'll kick off: i'm sofia, account exec on redwood, i'll be your main contact for contracting and pricing.
[00:17] Liam: liam chen, solutions engineer — i'll be the tech lead on the redwood side for the pilot and infra setup.
[00:21] Ava: ava martinez, customer success manager — i'll own onboarding and runbooks.
[00:25] Maya: maya thompson, head of engineering at crestfield.
[00:28] Raj: raj patel, cto.
[00:30] Elena: elena garcia, devops.
[00:31] Noah: noah reed, security.
[00:33] Priya: priya singh, product.

[02:10] Sofia: great, thanks. quick agenda — intro, scope the pilot, discuss deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), security and compliance items, benchmarks and SLOs, and then next steps. anything to add?
[02:20] Raj: maybe run through the baseline infra reqs — latency targets and data residency.
[02:25] Sofia: sure.

[04:00] Maya: high level — we want to pilot a clinician-facing assistant that helps summarize notes and answer basic queries from EHR text. priority is accuracy and privacy; latency is important but not patient-critical for the first pilot. default users will be clinicians and case managers.
[04:20] Priya: i'd add we need to measure hallucination rates on 200 clinical prompts and have automatic rejection when confidence below threshold.
[04:28] Liam: okay makes sense. For the pilot we usually recommend Redwood hosted API to reduce ops friction; we can also run dedicated pools if you need predictable throughput or want to isolate data. For full private deployment we have VPC/private on-prem options — that adds more setup time.

[06:15] Elena: our compliance bar is SOC2 and we also need customer-managed KMS for keys if possible. we also have strict audit log needs. do you support SSO/SAML?
[06:29] Ava: yes — SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported. for KMS we integrate with common providers and HSMs, we'll provide docs.
[06:35] Noah: also need encryption at rest with customer keys and retention controls.
[06:38] Liam: we support bring-your-own-key patterns and can enable encrypted KV cache as well, though i should flag that some of the KV cache metrics are slightly different in private setups.
[06:47] Noah: ok noted — we'll need the implementation details.

[08:00] Sofia: timeline-wise — customers typically run a 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding + sandbox, week 1 bench + eval, week 2 iterate prompts and model config, week 3 production roll small cohort. does that work?
[08:14] Maya: yes that aligns. we have internal timeline to present to executive team on 12/20 so this works.

[10:05] Liam: on benchmarking — we'll run two primary tests: latency/cost profile and quality evals. latency: we'll collect p50/p95/p99 under expected concurrency (we should confirm expected qps). For cost we'll run token-usage simulations on your prompts. For quality, we recommend a 200-prompt set with ground truth and simple metrics (exact match, factuality).
[10:34] Priya: on concurrency, initial expected qps is low — 2-5 qps during clinic hours, burst to 15 qps.
[10:40] Liam: that is small, so even hosted can handle it easily; dedicated is optional if you want reserved throughput.

[12:12] Raj: what about model choices? we saw your model catalog — any recommendations?
[12:18] Liam: for clinical summarization we recommend a medium-sized model with instruction-tuning. Redwood's catalog has a few open models we've verified; if you want lower latency/cost we can recommend a quantized variant. Also we can do rollouts — canary to smaller model and fallback to higher-quality when needed.
[12:38] Maya: do you support function-calling or structured output so we can parse summaries into fields?
[12:44] Liam: yes, function calling and structured JSON outputs are supported; we'll share examples in the runbook. sometimes the transcription/prod docs show redwood product names as 'Red-serve' in auto transcripts, so apologies if that shows up.

[15:00] Elena: network wise — if we go hosted, is there a way to pin region and control egress? we have data residency constraints for some states.
[15:10] Ava: yes — hosted supports region selection and policy-based routing. for stricter residency we recommend a VPC/private deployment.

[16:40] Noah: on audit logs and retention, do you provide per-request logs and the ability to redact PII automatically?
[16:48] Liam: we emit detailed traces and per-request metadata; we also have a PII redaction pipeline we can enable in the ingest path. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[19:12] Priya: how long does a VPC deployment take vs dedicated?
[19:18] Sofia: dedicated reserved capacity is faster — a few days to provision and configure. VPC/private can take several weeks depending on networking approvals and on-prem. pilot usually starts on hosted and then migrates.

[21:30] Maya: cost sensitivity is real — what's typical pilot cost?
[21:35] Sofia: pilots vary; for your expected qps and 200 prompts we'd estimate X dollars for tokens and a small reserved dev pool if you want dedicated trial. I'll send a proper pricing sheet; rough ballpark is in the pricing doc i will attach.

[23:00] Liam: technical note: for EHR summarization we recommend enabling prefix caching and using KV cache for repeated patient contexts; it can reduce token usage significantly. but if you require customer-managed keys we need a bit of config for encrypted cache.

[25:05] Maya: ok that sounds good.

[27:40] Sofia: let's clarify success metrics for the pilot — suggested: latency p95 under 350ms for single-turn queries, hallucination rate under X% on curated set, and cost per consult below target; what do you think?
[27:55] Priya: yes hallucination threshold is important; we'll quantify after we provide the 200 prompts.

[30:00] Liam: i'll prepare a benchmark plan: test harness, sample prompts, concurrency patterns, and a scoring sheet. we'll also propose model/config combos and quantization profiles.

[31:45] Noah: one more security item — our legal team will want to see subprocessors and data flow diagrams.
[31:52] Ava: we'll include a data flow diagram and subprocessors list in the security pack.

[34:10] Sofia: ok final recap: redwood sends security docs + SOC2 by 11/25, pricing and pilot agreement by 11/27, redwood to provision sandbox and API keys after contract, liam schedules infra deep-dive with elena and team week of 11/30, crestfield provides 200 de-identified prompts by 11/29.

[36:00] Raj: sounds good. who owns contract discussions?
[36:05] Sofia: i'll own commercial terms; legal will loop in if any redlines — i'll include payment and PO flow.

[38:20] Priya: any recommended guardrails for clinical use?
[38:28] Liam: yes — temperature control, system prompts for guardrails, and automated rejection on low confidence; also always include human-in-loop for any diagnosis related outputs. we'll share default guardrail configs.

[40:10] Elena: for network we need an allowed IP list; can you provide IP ranges?
[40:15] Ava: yes we'll send published egress IP ranges and region endpoints.

[42:00] Maya: ok one last thing — can we run a small smoke test with obfuscated data before sharing the full prompt set?
[42:06] Liam: absolutely. we can run a quick smoke on the sandbox within 48 hours of provisioning.

[44:10] Sofia: wrapping up — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the security pack and pricing; liam will send an invite for the infra deep-dive. any final q's?
[44:22] Noah: none from security.
[44:25] Priya: thanks.
[44:27] Sofia: great — talk soon.

[46:00] meeting end
